questions.worked_solution:
First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{1-3x}{x(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+2}+\frac{C}{(x+2)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(x+2)^{2}$ and get

$$
1-3x=A(x+2)^{2}+B(x)(x+2)+C(x).
$$

Plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-3(0) & =A(0+2)^{2}+B(0)(0+2)+C(0) \\ 1 & =4A \\ A & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-3(-2) & =A(-2+2)^{2}+B(-2)(-2+2)+C(-2) \\ 7 & =-2C \\ C & =-\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-3x & =A(x+2)^{2}+B(x)(x+2)+C(x) \\ 1-3(1) & =A(1+2)^{2}+B(1)(1+2)+C(1) \\ -2 & =9A+3B+C \\ -2 & =9(\frac{1}{4})+3B+(-\frac{7}{2}) \\ B & =-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1-3x}{x(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{1}{4x}-\frac{1}{4(x+2)}-\frac{7}{2(x+2)^{2}}
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1-3x}{x(x+2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{4x}-\frac{1}{4(x+2)}-\frac{7}{2(x+2)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x-\frac{7}{2}\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+\frac{7}{2(x+2)}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

questions.worked_solution:
Let's first factor the denominator of the integrand:

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}+13x+8}{{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+4x}=\frac{5{x}^{2}+13x+8}{x(x+2)^{2}}
$$

We must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}+13x+8}{x(x+2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+2}+\frac{C}{(x+2)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(x+2)^{2}$ and get

$$
5{x}^{2}+13x+8=A(x+2)^{2}+Bx(x+2)+Cx.
$$

Plugging in $x=-2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-2)^{2}+13(-2)+8 & =A(-2+2)^{2}+B(-2)(-2+2)+C(-2) \\ 2 & =-2C \\ C & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(0)^{2}+13(0)+8 & =A(0+2)^{2}+B(0)(0+2)+C(0) \\ 8 & =4A \\ A & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=-1$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5(-1)^{2}+13(-1)+8 & =A(-1+2)^{2}+B(-1)((-1)+2)+C(-1) \\ 5-13+8 & =A-B-C \\ 0 & =2-B-(-1) \\ 0 & =-B+3 \\ B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}+13x+8}{{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+4x}=\frac{2}{x}+\frac{3}{x+2}-\frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5{x}^{2}+13x+8}{{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x}+\frac{3}{x+2}-\frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{(x+2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+\frac{1}{x+2}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.

questions.worked_solution:
First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-7}+\frac{B}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-7)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-7)^{3}$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-9x+16=A(x-7)^{2}+B(x-7)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=7,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(7)^{2}-9(7)+16 & =A(7-7)^{2}+B(7-7)+C \\ 2 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=6$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(6)^{2}-9(6)+16 & =A(6-7)^{2}+B(6-7)+C \\ -2 & =A-B+2 \\ A-B & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=8$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(8)^{2}-9(8)+16 & =A(8-7)^{2}+B(8-7)+C \\ 8 & =A+B+2 \\ A+B & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=-4$ and $A+B=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =-4+6 \\ A & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=6,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1+B & =6 \\ B & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}=\frac{1}{x-7}+\frac{5}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-7)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-9x+16}{(x-7)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-7}+\frac{5}{(x-7)^{2}}+\frac{2}{(x-7)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-7}\,\text{d}x+5\int \frac{1}{(x-7)^{2}}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{(x-7)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-7|-\frac{5}{x-7}-\frac{1}{(x-7)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's first factor the denominator of the integrand:

$$
\frac{x+1}{{x}^{2}+6x+9}=\frac{x+1}{(x+3)^{2}}
$$

We must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+3)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x+3}+\frac{B}{(x+3)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A$ and $B,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+3)^{2}$ and get

$$
x+1=A(x+3)+B.
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+1 & =A(-3+3)+B \\ B & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $B,$ we can solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+1 & =A(0+3)-2 \\ 1 & =3A-2 \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum:

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+3)^{2}}=\frac{1}{x+3}-\frac{2}{(x+3)^{2}}
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x+1}{(x+3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{x+3}-\frac{2}{(x+3)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|\,{|}_{0}^{1}+2\cdot \frac{1}{x+3}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+2(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})+2(-\frac{1}{12}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})-\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
